arguments.query: upload or attach a file to a folder / test case

produced.finding: No capability attaches a file to a FOLDER at all (only test-cases, test-results and test-plans have an attach path: link_attachments_to_test_case, list_entity_attachments). Even for those, the file-content half of the two-step flow (upload_generic_attachments / upload_ai_attachments) is explicitly documented as 'NOT INVOCABLE through this interface' because it reads a multipart file upload that cannot be expressed as a JSON MCP argument. With no files it silently returns 200 {generic_attachment: []} rather than erroring. So no attachment of any kind (folder or otherwise) can be created through this MCP surface.

notes: describeCapability declares a real committed shape, not a thin passthrough: 200 -> {success: boolean, attachments: [{id, name, content_type, key, product_id, byte_size, checksum, url, download_url}]} (each entry also gets a ready-formatted 'size' string per the guidance text, though it is not listed in the schema properties). Params are both path integers: project_id and folder_id, no query/body, no json_path nesting — this is a plain GET. Used the v1 integer project id (379335744) directly per the pool's guidance that v1 endpoints take the integer form; it worked first try against both fixture folders, so the PR-2005 v2 form was never needed. Invoked against __readonly__ (764093) and __scratch__ (764138): both returned HTTP 200 {success:true, attachments:[]} exactly as declared for an empty case. Per the task's own instruction, an empty collection proves nothing about the declared item shape (id/name/content_type/key/product_id/byte_size/checksum/url/download_url), so this cannot be scored PASS. Escalated per the task's fallback order: (1) checked both fixture folders directly (both empty); (2) used list_root_folders to see whether the __mcp-capability-fixture__ project (PR-2005 / 379335744) has any other, older folders that might already carry attachments -- it does not; the project contains exactly __readonly__ and __scratch__, nothing else, so there is no pre-existing account data anywhere in this project to inspect; (3) looked for a documented upload/attachment-create capability that could write a real attachment into __scratch__ -- none exists for folders, and the only capabilities that back test-case/result/plan attachments (upload_generic_attachments, upload_ai_attachments) are explicitly documented as not invocable through this MCP interface (multipart file bytes cannot be expressed as JSON arguments), so even a test-case-shaped workaround was unavailable. No write was attempted since there was nothing invocable to write with, and no user_permission was requested. Global search was deliberately not used to look for attachments elsewhere on the account, per the task's instruction about the 6-day indexing lag. Verdict: UNVERIFIED -- the capability responds exactly as declared for the wrapper ({success, attachments}) but the declared item shape inside `attachments` could not be checked against any real row, and no path exists (documented or invocable) to manufacture one.
